notes: Full description: pkix-lint/src/cabf_tls_br.rs lines 185-191 — the doc comment says 'a 2047-bit modulus is 256 bytes with a leading zero'. This is wrong. A 2047-bit modulus is 256 bytes total (ceil(2047/8)=256) and since the leading bit of a 2047-bit number is set at position 6 of the top byte (0b0xxxxxxx pattern), the high bit is 0, so NO leading 0x00 byte is added by DER unsigned encoding. A 2047-bit modulus is 256 bytes with NO leading zero. The check n_bytes >= 256 would pass for this 2047-bit key, meaning the lint has an off-by-one in the effective minimum. The doc comment's own statement two sentences earlier ('minimum 2048-bit modulus is 256 bytes with no leading zero') is also questionable — a true 2048-bit key has the MSB of the 256-byte modulus set, requiring a leading 0x00, making it 257 bytes in DER INTEGER. The acknowledged conservatism ('floor-byte comparison used by most CA/B Forum linting tools') means keys with moduli 2033-2047 bits pass the check. This is an existing acknowledged approximation, but the specific 2047-bit claim in the comment is incorrect. Fix: Correct the comment to accurately describe which key sizes pass and fail, and remove the wrong 2047-bit statement.
title: FINDING: RsaMinKeySizeLint doc comment has wrong 2047-bit claim
